title: The legacy key is Removed by D-RCV-35 (U1) while the Work Package still asks for an APP story under it, so the story states a withdrawal and a build in one document
source: Legacy RWB-DM-002 rows Status, Decision, Why, Read path instead, Data product and Withdrawn IDs (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3.md, file header lines 1-11 and the RWB-DM-002 section); Work Package B-P1-06 story line RWB-P1-DM002-APP; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 change note for version 3 and A2.2; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.10; Template and Rules v1 R-PREC (source precedence) and R6
section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 7 Acceptance criteria (closing note); section 9 State transitions; section 19 Out of scope
description: Two levels of the same key disagree. The legacy story master (precedence level 9) marks RWB-DM-002 Removed by D-RCV-35 (U1) and withdraws AC1 to AC3 and TC-DM-002-01 to TC-DM-002-04, because ACE ingests the SCBPDM customer, phone, e-mail and address data and holds the one copy. The FSD and TSD P1 v3 (precedence levels 7 and 6) are re-based on the same decision and remove the tables party and contact_point. The higher sources therefore win and the migration cannot be built. The Work Package B-P1-06 nevertheless lists RWB-P1-DM002-APP as an APP story to be written for this legacy key with two retained test case IDs and no legacy AC. The result is a story that must both record a withdrawal and deliver a build: the read path that replaces the migration. No source states that the replacement read path is the intent of the legacy key, and no source names the story that would own it if this one were retired instead.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-002 reads 'Status | Removed', 'Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1)', 'Withdrawn IDs | AC1 to AC3; TC-DM-002-01 to TC-DM-002-04'; the legacy file header reads 'Two stories leave because the data is already in ACE (RWB-DM-001, RWB-DM-002)'; the Work Package line reads "id": "RWB-P1-DM002-APP", "wt": "APP", "disposition": "Split (rework)", "acs": [], "tcs_legacy": ["TC-DM-002-01", "TC-DM-002-04"]; TSD P1 v3 T3.10 reads 'party | 13 | Copy of SCBPDM data (U1) | v_ace_customer; flags to party_ext' and 'contact_point | 8 | Copy of SCBPDM data (U1) | v_ace_contact; consent and quality to contact_point_ext'.
proposed: Keep the withdrawal and keep the story: confirm in the Change Register and the story catalog that RWB-P1-DM002-APP is the rework of the withdrawn key and delivers the read path only, that no extract, load, reconciliation or cutover is in its scope, and that its two retained test case IDs carry new text. If the programme prefers retirement, the read path must be moved to a named story of P1 before this one is closed, so that DP02 has an owner.

title: The read path that replaces the migration is described in one legacy row only: no source fixes the fields the answer carries, the join of a person to many contact points, or the use of the two extension tables beyond their column list
source: Legacy RWB-DM-002 row Read path instead; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.1.3.2 field catalog and A2.2 DP02 row; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.3 (v_ace_customer, v_ace_contact, v_ace_ca_relation), T3.5 (party_ext, contact_point_ext) and T3.9 (business-key links); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 37 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R7.3 (fill order) and R9
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 4 to 7; section 7 AC2 and AC4; section 11 Data; section 13 Database and migrations and Configuration and reference data
description: The replacement of the migration is given as one prose row ('v_ace_customer for the customer and the masked identity, v_ace_contact for phone, email and address, v_ace_ca_relation for the borrower, guarantor and co-borrower roles, and party_ext and contact_point_ext for the Workbench flags and consent'). It does not say which of the 20 customer fields, 9 contact fields and 5 relation fields an answer returns, whether an answer returns one row per contact_key or one row per person, which of the extension columns are read on the customer read path as opposed to a later screen, or how a person with no extension row is answered. The TSD gives the columns and the 1:1 cardinality (T3.5, T3.9) but no read-path shape, and the FSD field catalog lists the extension columns without saying which of them the customer read returns.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-002 'Read path instead | v_ace_customer for the customer and the masked identity, v_ace_contact for phone, email and address, v_ace_ca_relation for the borrower, guarantor and co-borrower roles, and party_ext and contact_point_ext for the Workbench flags and consent'; TSD P1 v3 T3.9 reads 'party_ext | person_key | v_ace_customer.person_key | 0 or 1 to 1' and 'contact_point_ext | contact_key | v_ace_contact.contact_key | 0 or 1 to 1'; TSD P1 v3 T3.5 gives the 12 and 14 columns with no read shape; FSD P1 A2.1.3.2 gives the flags and consent columns with no consumer named.
area: rwb-source-data customer and party read path
proposed: Fix the read-path answer in the contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP (the operation that serves it) as: the customer fields of v_ace_customer, one row per contact_key of v_ace_contact, one row per account of v_ace_ca_relation, the four party_ext flags as an optional object, and the consent and quality of each contact row; state that a person with no extension row is answered with the object absent and not with defaults. Keep the field names in the physical schema and the dictionary, not in code.

title: Where the masking of the ACE-sourced personal fields is answered is fixed in another service's story, while this story may declare no contract dependency and no masking pattern
source: Legacy RWB-DM-002 rows Read path instead and Why; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.1.3.1 (BR-P1-001-6) and the A2.15 identity-masking text; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 12, 14 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-08 and DP-11; Work Package B-P1-06 story line for RWB-P1-DM002-APP (C empty, patterns DP05 and DP15)
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 8; section 7 AC3 and AC6; section 8 BR3; section 10 Authority; section 13 Build steps
description: The masking of the ACE-sourced personal fields is decided in rwb-access (P4): the policy and masking rows are P4 data, the authorise contract answers masked or clear per field ID, and Architecture v5 says masking is applied by rwb-source-data. The Work Package fixes this story's contract dependencies as empty and its patterns as DP05 and DP15, so the story cannot declare the rwb-access authorise contract as a C dependency (DP-08) even though that is where the answer comes from. No source states which consumer applies the masked rendering of v_ace_contact.contact_value for the case screen, nor whether the answer of this service carries a masked rendering or only the raw value plus a marker.
evidence: FSD P1 v3 A2.15 reads 'Phone, email and address come in full from v_ace_contact, because notices and calls need them, and are masked at the API by role'; FSD P1 v3 BR-P1-001-6 reads 'A view never exposes customer.identification_number in clear; it returns id_no_masked and id_no_last4 only'; TSD P1 v3 T3.4 reads 'The identity number is never exposed in clear'; Architecture v5 slide 12 reads 'masking is applied by rwb-source-data'; RWB-P4-E1069-APP writes the masking rows and answers masking on POST /authorise; the Work Package line reads '"patterns": ["DP05", "DP15"], "C": []'.
proposed: Record in the Service Contract Catalog that the masking answer for an ACE-sourced field is taken by rwb-source-data on the rwb-access authorise decision, and add the contract dependency to the story or to the platform guard library at the next revision of the plan; until then the story applies the answer as the service standard and keeps the dependency row as the Work Package fixes it.

title: A wave 4 story is marked Ready to start Day 1 on a platform Flyway contract, and the readiness rule does not name the case
source: Work Package B-P1-06 story line for RWB-P1-DM002-APP (wave 4, ready Day 1, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON); Template and Rules v1 R5.6 (W-MAP), R5.7 rules 2, 3 and 8; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 6 INVEST check; section 13 Feature switch
description: The story sits in wave 4 by the W-MAP of business epic EP08, and its only build dependency is RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, a platform contract story of wave 0. Under R5.7 rule 8 a story ready on CON dependencies only is Day 1, so the metadata is internally consistent; what is not stated is whether a wave 4 story may start on Day 1, or whether Day 1 readiness is a statement about the dependency graph only. The service itself is wave 1 in the service table, which makes the wave 4 tag a business-epic tag and not a delivery wave. No source resolves the two readings.
evidence: Template and Rules R5.6 maps EP08 to wave 4 and R5.7 rule 8 reads 'Ready to start = "Day 1" if the story has only CON H dependencies'; the service table gives rwb-source-data wave 1; the Work Package line reads '"wave": 4, "ready": "Day 1", "H": ["RWB-PLT-E1044-CON"]'.
proposed: State in the Day-1 Work Allocation that Ready to start is computed from the dependency graph only, so a story whose business epic is wave 4 may be picked up on Day 1 when its build edges are platform contracts; and keep the wave tag as the business epic tag it is.

title: The read operation, its request and answer field names, and the feature switch of the read path are owned elsewhere or named by no source, while the story must still build and be switched
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 15 and 41; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.14 and A2.15; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T-A (endpoint inventory, absence of the customer read path); Work Package B-P1-06 story line for RWB-P1-DM002-APP; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and the R-PREC default ruling on feature flags
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1 and AC2; section 12.1 REST operations provided; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 13 Configuration and reference data and Feature switch
description: Three values the story needs are not in any source it may read. (1) The read of a customer and its parties is the operation GET /customers/{id} of rwb-source-data, which the Work Package assigns to RWB-P1-E1069-APP; this story therefore claims no path, no parameter and no response schema, but it still needs the answer field names to build the repository behind it, and the TSD endpoint inventory carries none of them. (2) The two preconditions of the read path (RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-P1-E1069-DB) are not build edges in the Work Package, so the story must be buildable from contract fakes on Day 1 and the plan records no edge. (3) The feature switch of the read path is a parameter of the platform flag library by the R-PREC default ruling, whose key, default and off behaviour no source names.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 15 (P1 contract) reads 'REST GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}; GET /collateral/{id}, /payments?accountId=; GET /freshness (business date); POST /business-days/{date}/ready (Airflow)'; the Work Package line reads '"H": ["RWB-PLT-E1044-CON"], "C": [], "X": []'; Template and Rules R3 default rulings give feature flags to the platform library; no extract names a flag key or an off behaviour.
proposed: Publish the customer and party answer schema in the RWB-P1-E1069-APP contract with its field names and its not-found and stale shapes; record RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-P1-E1069-DB as preconditions of this story in the Dependency Map without adding an H edge; and fix the read-path switch key and its off behaviour in the Service Template Specification.
